summary: Feed s089_single to IDS is degraded due to significant packet loss (7.8% of TCP packets show gaps). All other visibility checks (duplicates, encryption, VLANs, directionality, truncation, tunnels, oversize, tool overload) are healthy.

findings.root_cause: SPAN/mirror port oversubscription or packet broker buffer exhaustion causing random packet drops before the IDS. 198 of 2542 TCP packets (7.79%, threshold 1%) show missing sequence data, consistent with a congested SPAN session or overloaded broker ingress dropping under burst load rather than IDS overload (tool_overload is healthy).
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS requires complete bidirectional streams and full payload for signature matching and stream reassembly. With 7.8% gaps, TCP reassembly fails, signatures miss across packet boundaries, and attacks can evade detection resulting in false negatives and incomplete forensic evidence.

recommended_fix.why: Passive TAP does not drop packets under load like SPAN/mirror does and provides lossless, full-duplex capture. Replacing SPAN with TAP (with proper broker aggregation/capacity planning for the 1 Gbps IDS port) will eliminate the 7.8% loss and restore complete traffic to the IDS for reliable detection.
